findings.claim: The diff amended every mirror of the 'key unset => no_useful_hits can never fire' sentence; the shipped searchRelevanceFloor JSDoc still says 'UNSET = NO FLOOR: `no_useful_hits` and the spec refusal's below-floor arm can never fire', and the consumer list enumerates only the below-floor cause.
findings.counterexample: Executed: floor unset, one NaN hit => <retrieval-envelope status="no_useful_hits" method="hybrid" bestRelevance="n/a" floor="none" hits="0" faulted="1" />. The identical sentence at docs/wiki/config-reference.md WAS amended by this diff; the JSDoc in the package this changeset bumps was not.

findings.claim: Bumping @mmnto/mcp minor on the grounds that no cohort code parses the envelope; the envelope is a documented published contract ('parses with a single regular expression, so wrapper agents can route on retrieval confidence').
findings.counterexample: Measured: the repo's OWN wrapper regex in search-knowledge.test.ts (anchored hits="(\d+)" \/>) stops matching — 13 of the 24 old-reader failures are exactly this. packages/mcp/CHANGELOG.md records that the last change to this line (mmnto-ai/totem#2727) deliberately preserved the shape 'so the wrapper-agent single-regex contract holds'. @mmnto/mcp publishes to npm, so consumers outside the cohort exist by construction.

findings.claim: The all-faulted arm carries 'the CLI refusal's sentence' (singular), mirroring formatGroundingRefusal.
findings.counterexample: Executed: the body stated the cause TWICE — the first sentence then faultedDisclosure()'s 'did not count as signal or as exemption' line. In the CLI that second line lives only in the else/below-floor arm, never on the bestRelevance === null arm. It is also vacuous when every hit is faulted.

findings.claim: 'With no floor ... a negative or above-1 value was rendered as a measurement in the per-hit field, the envelope and the selection manifest.'
findings.counterexample: Executed against origin/main's reader: floor unset, hits [-0.1, 0.8] => the emitted manifest row's candidate reason is 'returned rank=1' and context carries no relevance. The manifest renders a relevance only inside 'below-relevance-floor ... relevance=...', which requires a floor. Inherited verbatim from the issue's Consequences.

findings.claim: A faulted hit 'is disclosed by path with `relevance faulted` rather than a number'.
findings.counterexample: Executed: exempt + faulted with no floor => status="ok" hits="2" faulted="1" and the faulted hit is RETURNED IN FULL with its content, field reading 'faulted (not a finite number in [0, 1])'. cross-repo-mesh.md states it correctly; the two docs disagreed.

findings.claim: Comment: 'Never rendered as a number a reader could compare' — the assertion is not.toMatch(/relevance (NaN|-0\.100|1\.500|Infinity)/).
findings.counterexample: Latent: the pattern is case-sensitive and space-delimited, so it cannot match the per-hit rendering '**Relevance:** 1.500'. No mutant escapes (the formatResult-prints-the-number mutant is killed by two other tests), so this is assertion hygiene, not a hole.

findings.claim: The it.each plus inner floor loop covers the invalid-value domain and both floor states.
findings.counterexample: Latent: Number.NEGATIVE_INFINITY is pinned only in core, and the all-faulted arm reached via min_relevance rather than a config floor is untested — it works (executed: min_relevance 0.7 with a lone NaN => no_useful_hits, floor="0.700", faulted="1"), but nothing pins it. The inner for-loop also does not name which iteration failed.

verdict: No BLOCKING defect: the three-class classification, the all-faulted arm's placement and gating, the manifest schema coupling and the floor semantics survived every constructed and executed counterexample, fault-free batches are byte-identical apart from faulted="0", 11 of the 12 new tests fail on origin/main's reader for the issue's own semantic reasons (13 pre-existing failures are attribute-only), and all 9 mutants were killed. Two MATERIAL items for the seat: a stale contract sentence left in shipped @mmnto/totem JSDoc (F1, folded) and a bump-level ruling on breaking the documented single-regex envelope contract as a minor (F2, put to the operator).
